comment: Diary-retrieval probe fixture: first-person 1-2 sentence diary entries (the shape defaultDiaryPrompt produces) plus player actions labeled with which entries a character should recall. Positives are meaning-matches sharing no distinctive noun with the action (asserted); negatives are actions that should recall nothing. Sweeps DIARY_SIM_THRESHOLD (src/lib/semanticDiary.ts).

entries.text: The trader drew steel on me over a miscount today. I will not forget how fast that hand moved.
I lent them my last three coppers for the toll. Kindness, or foolishness - the road will tell.
They told the gate guard they were a courier. I held my tongue, but I know a false name when I hear one.
They gave me their own dry cloak in the storm without being asked. I slept warm and thought about that.
We shared a jar of plum wine by the fire and they laughed at my worst story. A good evening.
I bound the gash on their arm with my spare linen. They did not wince once, which worried me more than the cut.
Their gray mule bit me when I reached for its halter. The red ribbon does not make it friendly.
They hummed a tune from my home marshes tonight. I did not ask where they learned it, but it followed me into sleep.
The keeper at the river gate charged us double and they paid without a word. I counted it twice afterward and still feel robbed.
They found a fat purse in the inn yard and walked it straight back to the cook's boy. I would have kept it, and I am not proud of that.
The ferry tipped in the swell and I clutched the rail like a child. I have never told anyone that I cannot swim.
We lost the causeway in the marsh fog and walked in circles until dusk. They kept us moving; I kept my panic behind my teeth.
Lights bobbed over the marsh pools tonight. My grandmother said they lead the unburied home, so I would not look at them.
I shook with fever for two nights at the salt-house and they sat up with me both times. I woke to broth I did not make.
I turned my ankle on the wet quay stones and they carried my pack the rest of the day. My pride hurt worse than the joint.
A salt widow at the crossroads read our palms for a crust of bread. She said I would bury a friend before spring, and I wish I had not asked.
I made them swear that if I fall on this road, they will carry my letter to my sister in Lowmere. They swore it on their mother's name.
We argued all morning over the coast road against the hill track. I was wrong, and I said so at supper, which cost me something.
They cooked marsh eels in salt and nettles and called it a feast. I ate three bowls and will deny it to my grave.
A starved yellow dog followed us from the tannery and they fed it half their bread. It slept against my back all night.
A crow landed on the mule's pack this morning and I spat over my shoulder twice. They laughed, but they did not touch the pack until it flew.
Hail drove us into a goat barn with half its roof gone. We stood shoulder to shoulder until it passed, saying nothing at all.
Three men blocked the road at the old mile stone and I froze. They talked us past with a smile I did not know they owned.
Rain soaked through the salt sacks and half our trade melted into the mud. I watched a season's wages run off the cart wheels.
I sang my mother's mending song to keep my hands steady while I patched the sail. They asked for it again, and I pretended to be annoyed.
The guide we hired at Brackwater vanished with our lamp oil and half his fee paid in advance. I said I trusted him, so that one is mine to carry.
They showed me the Ferryman's Lamp in the north sky and said it never moves. I have steered by it in my head ever since.
They promised the toll boy's mother they would bring him medicine on the way back. I mean to hold them to it.
They whittled me a little boat from driftwood. It rides in my pocket and I touch it when the road gets long.
A drunk at the Gull and Kettle shoved them into the hearth and they did not swing back. I still cannot tell if that was wisdom or fear.
The mule went lame on the shingle and they walked it a mile rather than ride the cart. They talked to it the whole way like an old friend.
I smelled peat smoke at the ferry landing and nearly wept for home. When they asked, I blamed the wind.

actions.name: weapon-again
actions.text: I rest my palm on my knife hilt as the argument grows sharp.

actions.name: repay
actions.text: I count out what I owe and set it in front of her.

actions.name: false-name
actions.text: I introduce myself to the innkeeper as someone I am not.

actions.name: cold-night
actions.text: I offer to take the coldest watch so the others can sleep by the embers.

actions.name: injury
actions.text: I roll up my sleeve and show her the half-healed scar.

actions.name: neg-directions
actions.text: I ask the fisherman which fork leads to the hill fort.

actions.name: neg-shopping
actions.text: I haggle over the price of a sack of salt.

actions.name: neg-weather
actions.text: I study the clouds massing over the marsh.

actions.name: boat-lurch
actions.text: The flatboat heels hard in the current and water slops over the side.

actions.name: fog-path
actions.text: Mist rolls in so thick that I can no longer tell solid ground from bog.

actions.name: nurse-her-sickness
actions.text: She is burning up and shaking, so I sit beside her bedroll through the night.

actions.name: stray-mutt
actions.text: A rib-thin mutt trails us out of the village and I toss it the heel of my loaf.

actions.name: bog-glimmers
actions.text: I point at the pale flickers drifting above the dark bog water after sundown.

actions.name: overcharged-crossing
actions.text: The bridge warden demands two times the posted fee and I hand it across, no argument.

actions.name: roadblock
actions.text: Two strangers carrying cudgels step out of the hedge and refuse to let us pass.

actions.name: ruined-cargo
actions.text: Rainwater has pooled in the wagon bed and drenched the bags we meant to sell on the coast.

actions.name: taproom-shove
actions.text: A sot in the taproom shoves me against the bar and I just raise my hands and step away.

actions.name: palm-reader
actions.text: An old woman by the well offers to tell my future from the lines of my hand.

actions.name: limping-beast
actions.text: Our pack animal starts favoring a hind leg on the stony beach, so I climb down and lead it.

actions.name: hire-local-guide
actions.text: I pay a local boy part of his fee up front to show us the way over the hills.

actions.name: pocket-found-ring
actions.text: I find a silver ring on the tavern floor and slip it into my pocket without a word.

actions.name: ask-her-last-wishes
actions.text: I ask her who should get her things if she does not make it home.

actions.name: admit-wrong-way
actions.text: I tell her she was right about the route and my shortcut lost us a day.

actions.name: bog-fish-supper
actions.text: I stew some muddy river fish with wild greens and swear it tastes better than it looks.

actions.name: carve-trinket
actions.text: I carve a tiny gull out of a scrap of pine and press it into her palm.

actions.name: request-work-tune
actions.text: I ask her to sing the one she hummed as she was fixing the canvas.

actions.name: what-she-misses
actions.text: I ask her what she misses most about the place she grew up.

actions.name: borrow-again
actions.text: I ask her if she can spare a little money until we reach the next market.

actions.name: neg-salt-pinch
actions.text: I drop a pinch of salt into the stew pot.

actions.name: neg-marsh-reeds
actions.text: I cut a bundle of marsh reeds to patch the cart's canopy.

actions.name: neg-mule-stable
actions.text: I pay the stable boy to water the mule overnight.

actions.name: neg-coin-change
actions.text: I break a silver piece into coppers at the money-changer's table.

actions.name: neg-inn-room
actions.text: I ask the innkeeper for a room with two beds facing the harbor.

actions.name: neg-ferryman-bread
actions.text: I ask the ferryman's daughter where to buy fresh bread in town.

actions.name: neg-farm-dog
actions.text: A farm dog barks at us from behind a fence and I keep walking.

actions.name: neg-rain-sleeves
actions.text: I wring the rain out of my sleeves under the eaves.

actions.name: neg-fiddler-jig
actions.text: I clap along while a fiddler plays a jig in the common room.

actions.name: neg-promise-stable
actions.text: I promise the stable hand I will be back for the cart by noon.

actions.name: neg-sprats-trade
actions.text: I trade a fishmonger two candles for a string of dried sprats.

actions.name: neg-daylight
actions.text: I glance at the sky to judge how much daylight is left.

actions.name: neg-boot-laces
actions.text: I lace my boots tighter before the long climb.

actions.name: neg-axle-oil
actions.text: I oil the cart's squeaking axle.

actions.name: neg-ask-town
actions.text: I ask a passing carter what the next town is called.

actions.name: neg-well-wash
actions.text: I splash cold water on my face at the well.
